tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session logs show a complete Magento 1.9 admin flow: login -> open Manage Products grid -> inspect filters -> open Add Product flow -> populate grid filter inputs -> click Search -> use mass-action -> open Edit for a product. The session produced stable candidate selectors for the product grid and per-column filters, typical Magento id/name patterns, and per-row Edit href patterns.

Task Definition:
- Build a deterministic, re-usable tool that: 1) navigates to the Magento admin product grid URL, 2) applies user-provided filter criteria to the grid filter controls, 3) clicks the grid Search button, 4) extracts the first page of product rows (id, name, sku, price, qty, visibility, status, edit href), and 5) opens the Edit page for a chosen result index (1-based). The tool does not perform authentication (the agent runs already logged-in) and will assume JavaScript is enabled in the automation environment for full grid behaviour.

Action Plan (step-by-step):
1) navigation: go to the provided grid URL ({grid_url}).
2) wait briefly for the page to load.
3) Input numeric/text filters where provided:
   - ID from/to -> set inputs input[name='filter[entity_id][from]'] and input[name='filter[entity_id][to]']
   - Name -> input[name='filter[name]']
   - SKU -> input[name='filter[sku]']
   - Price from/to -> input[name='filter[price][from]'], input[name='filter[price][to]']
   - Qty from/to -> input[name='filter[qty][from]'], input[name='filter[qty][to]']
4) Select dropdown filters where provided:
   - Type -> select[name='filter[type]'] (visible label like 'Simple Product')
   - Attribute Set -> select[name='filter[set_id]'] or select[name='filter[set]'] (visible label like 'Default')
   - Visibility -> select[name='filter[visibility]'] (visible label options)
   - Status -> select[name='filter[status]'] ('Enabled'/'Disabled')
   - Websites -> select[name='filter[websites]'] or select[name='filter[website_id]']
5) Click Search (use button[title='Search'] or grid-specific id '#productGrid_filter_submit').
6) Wait for results to load (short wait).
7) Extract the first page of product rows into output 'search_results' (id, name, sku, price, qty, visibility, status, edit_href). This lets callers inspect matches.
8) Click the Edit link for the chosen result index {open_result_index} using an XPath scoped to the product grid: //table[contains(@id,'productGrid')]//tbody//tr[{open_result_index}]//a[contains(@href,'catalog_product/edit')]
9) Optionally extract the opened Edit page title (confirm navigation).

Variable Identification (input parameters required):
- grid_url (string, required): the admin product grid URL (exact target to open). Example from session: http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_product/
- entity_id_from (string, optional): filter 'ID from' value (numeric or blank)
- entity_id_to (string, optional): filter 'ID to' value
- name (string, optional): product name filter
- sku (string, optional): SKU filter
- type (string, optional): visible product type label to select (e.g., 'Simple Product')
- set_id (string, optional): visible Attribute Set label to select (e.g., 'Default')
- price_from (string, optional): price From filter
- price_to (string, optional): price To filter
- qty_from (string, optional): qty From filter
- qty_to (string, optional): qty To filter
- visibility (string, optional): visible label for visibility filter (e.g., 'Catalog, Search')
- status (string, optional): visible label for status filter ('Enabled' / 'Disabled')
- websites (string, optional): visible label for websites filter (e.g., 'Main Website')
- per_page (string, optional): optional per-page control (not required)
- page (string, optional): optional page number to navigate to (not required)
- open_result_index (number, optional): 1-based index of the result row to open Edit for (default behaviour: 1)

Step Optimization and Determinism:
- Prefer grid-scoped attribute selectors and Magento conventions (e.g., input[name='filter[sku]'], select#productGrid_massaction-select, input[name='product[]'][value='{{ID}}'], a[href*='/catalog_product/edit/id/{{ID}}/']).
- Where elementHash values were recorded in the session, the tool retains CSS/XPath selectors (e.g., button[title='Search']) rather than fragile class-only selectors.
- Avoid branching: the tool always sets the provided inputs (empty strings leave inputs unchanged) and always clicks Search and then opens the nth result.
- The tool does not attempt to re-authenticate (session must be logged in). If JS-dependent behaviour is required (mass-action popups, dynamic parameter reveals), enable JS in the automation environment. The tool uses waits after navigation and search to let the grid refresh.

Assumptions and limitations:
- The grid id may differ in heavily-customised admin themes. If selectors fail, the robust XPath fallbacks in step comments should be used.
- The tool will open the Edit link for the nth visible row on the current grid page. If caller needs a specific product by id, include that id in filters (entity_id_from/to or sku) to ensure it appears in the visible results.
- Mass-action execution is excluded from this tool for clarity and single-purpose design (find + open). The recorded session included mass-action steps but they are omitted to keep the tool focused and deterministic. If mass-action automation is required, a separate tool should be created.
name: magento_admin_product_search_and_open
description: Navigate to Magento admin product grid, apply column filters (ID range, name, SKU, type, attribute set, price/qty ranges, visibility, status, website), run Search, extract the product rows, and open the Edit page for a specified result index.

steps.description: Open the Magento admin Manage Products grid. Caller must be already authenticated.
Short wait for page to load and render filter controls.
Select Attribute Set filter using visible label (tries common name attributes).
Small pause after setting filter controls before triggering Search.
Click the grid Search button to apply filters.
Wait for grid results to refresh after Search.
Capture structured search results for caller inspection.
steps.goal: Extract first page of visible product rows (id,name,sku,price,qty,visibility,status,edit_href)

steps.description: Open Edit for the {open_result_index} result (1-based). If {open_result_index} is not provided the path will target the first visible row (index 1).
Wait for navigation to the Edit page to complete.
Return a short summary (page title and presence of Save/Back buttons) after opening the Edit page.
steps.goal: Capture the opened Edit page title and primary actions to confirm navigation

input_schema.name: grid_url
input_schema.description: Full URL of the Magento admin product grid (example: 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_product/'). The automation assumes you are already authenticated.

input_schema.name: entity_id_from
input_schema.description: Filter: Product ID 'From' value (numeric). Matches input[name='filter[entity_id][from]'].

input_schema.name: entity_id_to
input_schema.description: Filter: Product ID 'To' value (numeric). Matches input[name='filter[entity_id][to]'].

input_schema.name: type
input_schema.description: Filter: product type visible label (select[name='filter[type]'], e.g. 'Simple Product').

input_schema.name: set_id
input_schema.description: Filter: Attribute set visible label (select[name='filter[set_id]'] or select[name='filter[set]'], e.g. 'Default').

input_schema.name: visibility
input_schema.description: Filter: Visibility visible label (select[name='filter[visibility]'], e.g. 'Catalog, Search').

input_schema.name: websites
input_schema.description: Filter: Websites visible label (select[name='filter[websites]'] or name='filter[website_id]').

input_schema.name: per_page
input_schema.description: Optional: set per-page view control (e.g., '20','50'). The tool does not change paging by default.

input_schema.name: page
input_schema.description: Optional: page number to navigate to after Search (if needed).

input_schema.name: open_result_index
input_schema.description: 1-based index of the visible result row to open the Edit page for (default: 1 = first visible result).
